articles.description: In a back-and-forth game laced with lead changes, Bryce Young rallied the Panthers to a 35-33 home win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday at Bank of America Stadium, a second straight victory for the 5-5 Panthers that padded lead in the NFC South.

article.story: ARLINGTON, Texas -- — When one touchdown became two and three and so on, all the way to six, Dak Prescott said the conversation was the same for the offense of the Dallas Cowboys: Just keeping doing it. So they did. Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran for a score, and the Cowboys reached the end zone on their first six drives while scoring on all eight possessions before kneeling once at the end of a 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. “It was just constant communication all game from all 11 of us, or whoever’s in the game, of keep pushing it, ‘We did it. We scored. Let’s go do it again,’” said Prescott, who tied his franchise record with 19 consecutive completions from early in the second quarter to early in the fourth. “Credit to all those guys, just their intensity, their focus.” Javonte Williams ran for a TD and caught one of Prescott's scoring passes while receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both had 100-yard days with a touchdown apiece. Lamb finished with 132 yards and Pickens had 102. Dallas (5-6) had never scored TDs on its first six possessions going back to at least 1993, as far back as the club said the statistic could be tracked. It was the Cowboys' first 50-point game since a 54-19 victory over Indianapolis on Dec. 4, 2022. The Titans scored five of the first six times they had the ball — two touchdowns and three field goals — in a matchup of the NFL's two worst defenses by yardage allowed. Tennessee (1-9) clinched a fifth consecutive losing season, the longest such streak since the franchise moved from Houston in 1997. “There’s a lot of things that need to change,” first-year coach Robert Saleh said. “Obviously it’s disgusting football. It’s embarrassing football. And obviously that starts with me.” One of the Tennessee TDs was Cam Ward's 59-yard pass to Carnell Tate when the receiver made the catch on the ground, got his rear end off the turf just before cornerback Cobie Durant touched him and ran to the end zone without anybody trying to tackle him. Ward had a 1-yard scoring run and a scrambling 12-yard TD toss to Calvin Ridley on fourth down in the final minute. The Titans had two early drives stall, which helped create a gap they couldn't close as the Cowboys rolled up 480 yards and 33 first downs, two shy of the club record. “Control what we can control. Continue to back the defense up. Continue to bring them life by scoring the football,” said Ward, who was 21 of 30 for 248 yards. “We didn’t have our best day today. We got stalled out in the red zone a couple of times. We had a turnover. At the end of the day, we’ve all got to help each other out.” Tate's score made it four consecutive weeks in which the Cowboys have allowed at least one touchdown of more than 50 yards. This time it was in the Dallas play-calling debut of veteran coach Mike Pettine, who took over those duties from 34-year-old Christian Parker, the youngest defensive coordinator in club history. Dallas scored at least 40 points for the second week in a row — but is 1-1 in those games. Parker was essentially demoted after a 46-40 loss to San Francisco in which the Cowboys gave up the most yards in a home game in franchise history (584). Pettine and Parker both worked from the sideline as the Cowboys forced the only two punts of the game, twice kept Tennessee out of the end zone on drives to at least the Dallas 20-yard line and sacked Ward five times.Team sacks leader Quinnen Williams had two. “The defense played well today,” coach Brian Schottenheimer said. “And that’s the players, the coaches. I thought (Parker and Pettine) were great together.” The touchdown streak for the Cowboys ended early in the fourth quarter, when they had to settle for Brandon Aubrey's 49-yard field goal and a 44-23 lead. Dallas got into the end zone again on Prescott's 2-yard touchdown pass to Brevyn Spann-Ford after Markquese Bell returned a fumble by Ward 70 yards to the Tennessee 15. Prescott finished 28 of 33 for 325 yards and a season-high 147.3 passer rating. Receiver KaVontae Turpin had a 22-yard scoring run as the Titans allowed at least 40 points for the third consecutive game. They have averaged 30 points per game in those three losses. “We have no choice but to get better,” Saleh said. “Surely it can’t get any worse.” Tony Pollard had 110 yards rushing in his first visit to Dallas since leaving the Cowboys for the Titans in free agency in 2024. Injuries Titans: S Tony Adams was ruled out in the first half due to an illness. ... CB Cor'Dale Flott (neck), S Terrell Burgess (knee) and LT Dan Moore Jr. (knee) were all hurt during the game.
